subject: Post-call: model recommendations + regression mitigation plan
content:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: model recommendations + regression mitigation plan

Sarah — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery so we can align the evals: 

- Goal: Replace parts of your summarization pipeline and improve long-form helpfulness in product docs search. Target throughput ~120 rps, 99th pct latency < 350ms.
- Data sensitivity: product docs include PII in some support tickets; will need SOC2 evidence and optional VPC.
- Success criteria: extractive accuracy > 88% on our internal QA set, human eval helpfulness >= your baseline.

My initial recommendations for model variants to evaluate (fast path -> high quality):
1) redwood-llama-13b-q4f32 (quantized) — best cost/latency; recommended for initial throughput testing.
2) redwood-13b-v1.9 (full FP16) — conservative quality baseline, historically stable for summarization.
3) open-llama-30b (v1) — higher quality ceiling, use for a smaller sample of critical docs.

Attached: acme_eval_benchmark.csv (seeded benchmarks we ran on a subset of your sample), prompt_sets_v2.zip (recommended prompts and scoring rubric), mutual_action_plan_ACME.pdf (proposed milestones + owners). Also pushed the full benchmark and prompt set to the Drive link above.

Important note on model versions: during today's call you mentioned encountering unexpected drop in candidate quality after a vendor update last month. We have a related internal incident: a rolling kernel change to redwood-llama-13b-v2 caused a subtle decoding difference in our FP16 path. We flagged this on Jun 4 — that change can show up as reorderings/verbosity shifts on long summaries.

Mitigation options we propose for your eval: 
- Pin to redwood-13b-v1.9 for the full production-like run (zero-change baseline).
- Run a focused regression check: compare v1.9 vs v2 on 200 critical docs (we've included a diff script in the Drive link).
- If you need higher throughput and are ok with slight quality variance, use the q4f32 quantized variant behind canary routing with a 5% sample.

Next steps I suggest: 
1) You confirm which evaluation set to use (we recommended sample A in the Drive).
2) We schedule a 30-min technical sync next week (I can bring Monica for infra + Rishi for model ops).
3) Decide whether to pin to v1.9 for initial rollout or try v2 behind canary.

Can you confirm timelines? If you're comfortable, I'll ask Rishi to prepare a short regression diff and rollback runbook.

— Ben

Ben / Monica — quick update on the regression side. I ran a 200-doc diff between redwood-13b-v1.9 and redwood-llama-13b-v2 using our regression harness. Findings: 
- Automated ROUGE / BLEU style stats show a small but measurable drop: mean ROUGE-L -3.8 pts, accuracy on extraction tests -4.1 pts.
- The qualitative gap is most visible on long-context ticket threads where v2 tends to expand on non-essential parts and sometimes introduces hallucinated steps.
- Root cause: the v2 kernel change altered top-k sampling cutoff threshold slightly in the FP16 path; we have a micro-patch that restores previous behavior.

Recommendation: For Acme's production-like eval, pin to redwood-13b-v1.9 as the authoritative baseline. Simultaneously we can run a canary with v2 on 5% of traffic after applying the micro-patch — that will let us validate perf gains without exposing all users to variance.

I attached a brief regression summary to the Drive link and included a short diff CSV (rows: doc_id, v1.9_summary, v2_summary, rouge_l_delta). Will push the detailed CSV to the shared Drive by EOD.

If Acme wants an immediate rollback for their dedicated capacity, the rollback is straightforward (pin node images to v1.9 and restart; can be executed within a 2-hour maintenance window).

— Rishi
Senior MLOps Engineer, Redwood Inference
